seo.title: Homeless help in Chicago - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified Chicago help for people experiencing homelessness: shelter intake, meals, showers, health care, benefits, jobs, IDs, legal help, youth, veterans, and pets.

page.heading: Chicago homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire, police, or ambulance: 911 Shelter request and city services: 311 or 312-744-5000 Food, health, and social-service referrals: 211 Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988 Domestic violence: 877-863-6338
page.notice: Beds, waiting areas, schedules, meals, costs, and eligibility can change. Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees shelter, housing, treatment, benefits, money, or a job the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
page.intro: If you need shelter tonight, call 311 and write down the service-request number. Single adults age 25 and older may also go to SPARC. Families with children may go to Shield of Hope/EHARC. A shelter request is not immediate housing: capacity is limited, and waits can last days or weeks. Tell the worker about children, pregnancy, age, disability, medical needs, domestic violence, pets, and your current location. — #shelter--sparc-24-hour-intake-for-single-adults-age-25 — #shelter--shield-of-hope-eharc-families-with-children

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for violence in progress, serious injury, trouble breathing, unconsciousness, overdose, fire, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location first.
City of Chicago guidance on 311 and 911

entries.title: 311 — shelter request and well-being check
entries.description:
Phone: 311 inside Chicago or 312-744-5000.
Ask for emergency shelter, a homeless outreach team, warming or cooling information, or a well-being check. Write down the service-request number and update 311 if your location or safety changes.
Chicago Coalition to End Homelessness — how to request help

entries.title: 211 Metro Chicago — 24-hour referrals
entries.description:
Call: 211; text: your ZIP code to 898211. — sms:898211
Multilingual referrals for food, shelter, health care, mental health, substance-use treatment, utility help, employment, and other services throughout Chicago and Cook County.
211 Metro Chicago

entries.title: Street Medicine and outreach — The Night Ministry
entries.description:
Street Medicine: 773-256-7549. Health Outreach Bus and case management: 773-372-3953.
Mobile teams provide health care, food, hygiene supplies, harm reduction, case management, and connections to shelter and housing at scheduled neighborhood and CTA stops.
Current outreach, bus, library, and CTA schedule

entries.title: Extreme heat and cold
entries.description:
Call 311 for the current warming or cooling location and hours. City warming areas are generally activated at 32°F or below; cooling measures depend on the city emergency plan.
Do not rely on an old address during severe weather. Tell 311 if a person cannot travel safely, needs a wheelchair-accessible option, or appears confused, hypothermic, or overheated.
Extreme-weather guidance

entries.title: Behavioral-health crisis
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours. For immediate physical danger or a medical emergency, call 911.
For an eligible nonviolent mental-health emergency without weapons, overdose, active substance use, or a medical problem, call 911 and ask whether a CARE behavioral-health response is appropriate.
Chicago CARE crisis-response program

entries.title: SPARC — 24-hour intake for single adults age 25+
entries.description:
Phone: 773-526-3707. Hours: 24 hours daily.
Walk-in shelter-placement intake with food, showers, and limited overflow space while a person waits. Capacity is about 200; when full, both waiting areas close. Call before traveling if possible.
Emergency-shelter intake guidance
entries.address: Address: 2241 South Halsted Street, Chicago, IL 60608

entries.title: Shield of Hope / EHARC — families with children
entries.description:
Families with children may walk in to request shelter assessment and temporary accommodation while staff seek the program that fits the family. Space is limited.
Bring documents if available, but ask for help even if they are missing. Tell staff immediately about domestic violence, pregnancy, disability, medications, or a safety concern.
Chicago family shelter intake
entries.address: Address: 924 North Christiana Avenue, Chicago, IL 60651

entries.title: Coordinated Entry System — housing assessment
entries.description:
Phone Access Point: 312-971-4178.
A housing assessment can match a person experiencing homelessness with eligible supportive or subsidized housing opportunities. It is not emergency shelter and does not guarantee housing or a short wait.
Coordinated Entry overview and access points

entries.title: Pacific Garden Mission
entries.description:
Phone: 312-492-9410.
Faith-based shelter, meals, clothing, and recovery support for adults. Call or arrive to ask about the current intake process and capacity. Religious services are part of the program and precede public meals.
Pacific Garden Mission — get help
entries.address: Address: 1458 South Canal Street, Chicago, IL 60607

entries.title: Franciscan Outreach shelters
entries.description:
Operates low-barrier shelters with three meals, case management, showers, storage, medical and behavioral-health connections. One program serving people moving from encampments has a room for personal pets.
Franciscan Outreach — shelter services
entries.how_to_access: Access: start with 311 or SPARC; do not travel to a shelter expecting direct entry unless staff confirm placement.

entries.title: Lincoln Park Community Services
entries.description:
Interim housing with meals, showers, laundry, clothing, toiletries, referrals, and case management. The organization does not promise walk-in shelter placement.
Immediate shelter request: call 311. Ask the coordinated-entry worker or shelter-placement team whether LPCS is an available match.
Lincoln Park Community Services

entries.title: Sarah's Circle — women age 18+
entries.description:
Phone: 773-728-1014. Drop-in hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Two meals, showers, laundry, clothing, hygiene supplies, mail, computers, and case management for single unaccompanied women, including trans women. Its interim shelter has limited placement; daytime entry does not guarantee a bed.
Sarah's Circle services
entries.address: Daytime center: 4838 North Sheridan Road, Chicago, IL 60640

entries.title: Covenant House Illinois — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 312-759-7878. Hours vary by day and may change.
Housing and shelter linkages, food, showers, laundry, clothing, mail, storage, charging, internet, ID help, education, employment, and counseling for young adults.
Covenant House Illinois — current hours
entries.address: Drop-in center: 2934 West Lake Street, Chicago, IL 60612

entries.title: The Night Ministry — emergency youth housing
entries.description:
Short-term emergency housing, ages 18–24: 877-286-2523. Youth outreach: 773-506-3122.
Emergency and longer-term housing connections for young people, plus outreach and case management. Call to screen for the correct program and current capacity.
The Night Ministry — youth resources

entries.title: Ignite — youth crisis and shelter
entries.description:
24-hour crisis line: 866-803-8336; text: 312-625-1858. — sms:+13126251858
Drop-in services, youth shelter, housing, education, employment, and support for young people. Call or text to enroll and confirm the most appropriate location.
Ignite locations and intake

entries.title: Greater Chicago Food Depository — find nearby food
entries.description:
Search current food pantries, groceries, and meal programs by address or ZIP code. Each partner controls its own hours, documents, and distribution limits.
Before traveling: call the listed pantry to confirm that it is open, serving your ZIP code, and has food available.
Find Food map

entries.title: Pacific Garden Mission — three daily meals
entries.description:
Phone: 312-492-9410.
Free hot breakfast, lunch, and dinner every day for adults and families who come to the mission. A Christian gospel service is held before each meal. Call for current meal times.
Pacific Garden Mission — food and clothing
entries.address: Address: 1458 South Canal Street, Chicago, IL 60607

entries.title: Inspiration Corporation — made-to-order breakfast
entries.description:
Enrollment contact: 312-626-6365.
Breakfast five days a week, drop-in support, and case management for people experiencing homelessness or poverty. Contact the program for the current location, schedule, and enrollment process.
Inspiration Corporation — get help

entries.title: Breakthrough Daytime Support Centers
entries.description:
Food, safe indoor space, showers, laundry, clothing, computers, notary service, and housing and employment support. Men's phone: 773-346-1785; women's phone: 872-444-8255.
Breakthrough — current services
entries.address: Men's Center: 402 North St. Louis Avenue, Chicago, IL 60624 Women's Center: 3330 West Carroll Avenue, Chicago, IL 60624
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3 p.m.; closed holidays and every third Tuesday.

entries.title: Sarah's Circle — breakfast and lunch for women
entries.description:
Two meals each weekday with showers, laundry, hygiene, mail, computers, and case management for women age 18 and older. Walk-ins are accepted, subject to capacity.
Sarah's Circle
entries.address: Address: 4838 North Sheridan Road, Chicago, IL 60640

entries.title: The Night Ministry Health Outreach Bus — meal at each stop
entries.description:
The mobile clinic distributes food and hygiene supplies with medical care and case management at neighborhood stops. The schedule includes Pilsen, New City, South Shore, and rotating city locations.
Phone: 773-372-3953. Check the live schedule because all stops and times can change.
Outreach Bus schedule

entries.title: 211 food referrals
entries.description:
Call: 211; text: your ZIP code to 898211. — sms:898211
Ask for a hot meal available today, a food pantry near your location, dietary accommodations, or help applying for SNAP. Confirm a distribution before making a long trip.
211 Metro Chicago directory

categories.title: Showers, laundry, clothing, mail, storage, and internet

entries.title: SPARC — showers and waiting space
entries.description:
Phone: 773-526-3707. Open 24 hours for single adults age 25 and older seeking shelter placement.
Provides showers, food, and limited overflow space during intake. When capacity is reached, the waiting areas close, so call first.
SPARC intake information
entries.address: Address: 2241 South Halsted Street, Chicago, IL 60608

entries.title: Breakthrough — showers, laundry, clothing, computers, and notary
entries.description:
Adults age 18 and older can ask for food, showers, laundry, clean clothing, computers, notary service, and a needs assessment.
Breakthrough Daytime Support Centers
entries.address: Men: 402 North St. Louis Avenue Women: 3330 West Carroll Avenue
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3 p.m., except holidays and every third Tuesday.

entries.title: Sarah's Circle — women age 18+
entries.description:
Weekday showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, winter coats, computers, mail address, two meals, and case management. Hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Sarah's Circle Daytime Support Center
entries.address: Address: 4838 North Sheridan Road, Chicago, IL 60640

entries.title: Covenant House — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Showers, laundry, hygiene products, clothing, food, mail, storage, internet, charging, transit passes, ID help, and case management. Call 312-759-7878 for today's hours.
Youth Drop-In Center
entries.address: Address: 2934 West Lake Street, Chicago, IL 60612

entries.title: Chicago Public Library — computers, Wi-Fi, charging, and information
entries.description:
Libraries provide free Wi-Fi and public computers; some services require a library card or guest pass. Staff can help locate city information but do not control shelter placement.
The Harold Washington Library Center at 400 South State Street also hosts scheduled homeless outreach and legal clinics. Check hours and room before traveling.
Chicago Public Library locations and hours

entries.title: Mail and safe document storage
entries.description:
Sarah's Circle and Covenant House publish mail service for eligible guests. Shelter and day-center case managers may also let you use an agency address for ID, benefits, or employment.
Ask how long mail is held, what identification is required to collect it, and whether the address may be used on official forms. Keep photographs of important documents in a protected account when possible.
Chicago Coalition to End Homelessness Law Project

entries.title: Medical emergency
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for trouble breathing, severe chest pain, unconsciousness, seizure, serious bleeding, overdose, or another life-threatening problem. Do not wait for a clinic appointment.
City of Chicago guidance on 311 and 911

entries.title: Heartland Alliance Health — primary, dental, mental-health, and substance-use care
entries.description:
Appointments: 773-275-2586. Care is offered regardless of ability to pay; clinics also provide outreach in shelters, transitional housing, encampments, and streets.
Clinic hours and services
entries.address: Broadway Clinic: 4009 North Broadway, Chicago, IL 60613 Englewood Clinic: 5501 South Halsted Street, Chicago, IL 60621

entries.title: The Night Ministry — free mobile health care
entries.description:
Street Medicine: 773-256-7549. Health Outreach Bus: 773-372-3953.
Wound care, health assessment, chronic-disease support, food, hygiene supplies, harm reduction, case management, and referrals at street, neighborhood, and CTA locations.
Outreach and Health program

entries.title: 988 and Illinois CARES
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours. Illinois CARES mobile-crisis line: 800-345-9049.
Free crisis support and connection to local mental-health or substance-use care. Call 911 when there is an active medical emergency, weapon, violence, or immediate threat to life.
Illinois CARES crisis information

entries.title: Chicago CARE behavioral-health response
entries.description:
For an eligible nonviolent mental-health crisis, call 911 and ask for the CARE Team. City clinicians and emergency medical technicians can de-escalate, assess, refer, and transport to community care.
CARE is not used for weapons, violence, overdose, active substance use, a medical emergency, or an active suicide attempt. The dispatcher decides the response.
CARE eligibility and hours

entries.title: Illinois Helpline — alcohol and other drugs
entries.description:
Call: 833-234-6343; text: HELP to 833234, 24 hours. — sms:833234
Confidential treatment navigation and immediate Medication Assisted Recovery support for opioid or alcohol use. In a suspected overdose, call 911 and use naloxone if available.
Illinois Helpline

entries.title: Free naloxone
entries.description:
Cook County Health and Chicago partners distribute free naloxone, including at the CORE Center, 2020 West Harrison Street. Chicago Public Library and CDPH locations may also carry kits.
Naloxone can wear off before the opioid does. Always call 911 after giving it and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
Free naloxone locations and overdose guidance

entries.title: Free STI and HIV services
entries.description:
Chicago Department of Public Health offers free STI/HIV testing and STI treatment at specialty clinics. Howard Brown also publishes free confidential community testing schedules.
If an HIV exposure was within the last 72 hours, ask immediately about PEP; do not wait for a routine testing day.
Chicago STI/HIV services | Howard Brown testing schedule — https://howardbrown.org/service/community-testing-sites-outreach-services/

entries.title: Illinois ABE — SNAP, Medicaid, and cash assistance
entries.description:
DHS Help Line: 800-843-6154. Apply online, by phone, or at a Family Community Resource Center.
The same application can request SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or refugee cash assistance, and Medicare Savings Programs. Ask for and save the case number.
ABE benefits application | Application help and phone numbers — https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/medicaidguide/contacts.html

entries.title: SNAP help for people experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Greater Chicago Food Depository benefits staff can explain SNAP rules and documents. A person without a fixed address can use a collateral statement as proof of Illinois residency.
Eligibility and work requirements changed in 2026. Ask staff to screen for exemptions rather than assuming you are ineligible.
SNAP/Link benefits help

entries.title: Chicago Coalition Law Project — benefits problems
entries.description:
Free helpline: 800-940-1119, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
Legal help with SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, SSI disability, benefit denials or termination, birth certificates, housing, family law, and other issues for people who are homeless or unstably housed.
Law Project

entries.title: Homelessness Prevention and rental assistance
entries.description:
Call 311 or 312-744-5000 and ask for “rental assistance” or the Homelessness Prevention Program.
One-time aid may help with rent, a security deposit, utilities, or another documented crisis for an eligible Chicago resident who still has housing. Funding and application periods are limited.
Emergency financial assistance

entries.title: Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
entries.description:
RAP is for Chicago residents who currently have housing but may lose it because of an eligible loss of income or emergency. It is open regardless of immigration status, subject to program rules and funds.
Call 311 or visit a DFSS Community Service Center for help in your language. It is not an emergency-shelter program.
Chicago Rental Assistance Program

entries.title: Cara Collective — job training and placement
entries.description:
Recruitment: 312-798-3309. If you have no phone or email, call or visit to discuss another contact method.
Work-readiness training, coaching, transitional jobs, professional clothing, and placement. A valid work-authorizing ID and Social Security card are required before job placement; staff publish other participation rules.
Apply to Cara
entries.address: Downtown Campus: 237 South Desplaines Street, Chicago, IL 60661

entries.title: Inspiration Kitchens — free food-service training
entries.description:
Free 12-week program for eligible low-income adults age 18+, including ServSafe certification, résumé and job-search support, transportation help, four weeks of paid training, and a possible paid transitional job.
Training is in person four days a week. Apply through the program; enrollment is not immediate employment.
Inspiration Kitchens job training
entries.address: Training location: 3504 West Lake Street, Chicago, IL

entries.title: StreetWise vendor income
entries.description:
Phone: 773-334-6600. Orientation published: Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10 a.m.
Vendor training, badge, selling-location help, and ten free starter magazines. Vendors buy later magazines and keep the difference when sold. Confirm orientation before traveling.
Become a StreetWise vendor
entries.address: Office: 2009 South State Street, Chicago, IL 60616

entries.title: Breakthrough employment support
entries.description:
Day-center staff provide employment training and connections alongside computers, clothing, showers, laundry, food, and housing help.
Visit Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3 p.m., except holidays and every third Tuesday. Ask whether you need an appointment for employment services.
Breakthrough services
entries.address: Men: 402 North St. Louis Avenue Women: 3330 West Carroll Avenue

entries.title: American Job Centers
entries.description:
Free public workforce centers offer job search, résumés, computers, skills assessment, training information, and employer connections. Services and appointment rules vary by site.
Use the official locator or ask 211 for the closest open center. Bring ID and work documents if available, but ask what can begin while documents are being replaced.
Chicago Cook Workforce Partnership — job seekers

entries.title: Free Illinois State ID with Homeless Status Certification
entries.description:
An eligible applicant can receive a free standard Illinois ID by presenting a notarized Homeless Status Certification completed within 90 days by an authorized agency or professional.
The form replaces the residency document, not proof of name, date of birth, or Social Security number. Ask a shelter, day center, attorney, school homeless liaison, or other authorized provider to complete it and help gather the remaining documents.
Homeless Status Certification form

entries.title: Free birth-certificate clinic — Harold Washington Library
entries.description:
Published schedule: Thursdays, 10 a.m.–1 p.m., with listed holiday exceptions; first come, first served and capacity-limited.
Free U.S. birth-certificate assistance for people experiencing homelessness. Be ready with your date and place of birth and parents' names. Check current clinic dates before traveling.
Law Project clinic calendar
entries.address: Address: 400 South State Street, 7th floor, Chicago, IL 60605

entries.title: Chicago CityKey — free municipal ID
entries.description:
Free optional Chicago government ID that can also work as a library card, Ventra card, and prescription-discount card. Apply online or at a scheduled printing event.
Proof of identity and Chicago residency are required; the document guide lists alternatives. Ask a service provider how to document residency if you have no fixed address.
How to apply for CityKey

entries.title: Chicago Coalition Law Project
entries.description:
Helpline: 800-940-1119, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
Free legal help for ages 14–24, adults, and families who are homeless or unstably housed: IDs, benefits, housing, family law, education, consumer problems, civil rights, and record sealing.
Legal clinics and help

entries.title: Legal Aid Chicago
entries.description:
Free civil legal assistance subject to income, location, case type, and capacity. Areas include housing, public benefits, family safety, consumer, employment, and other civil matters.
Use the intake page to check current phone and online options. For criminal arrest help, ask for a public defender or call the First Defense Legal Aid hotline listed by the Coalition.
Legal Aid Chicago — get help

entries.title: Rights while unsheltered
entries.description:
Keep your shelter-request number, photograph important papers, and ask for a written receipt if property is taken. Do not sign a form you do not understand; request language or disability accommodation.
For legal help after an encampment action, property loss, discrimination, or benefits problem, call the Coalition Law Project at 800-940-1119.
Chicago Coalition outreach and know-your-rights information

categories.title: Women, youth, LGBTQ+, immigrants, and veterans

entries.title: Domestic Violence Hotline — 24 hours
entries.description:
Call: 877-863-6338; TTY 877-863-6339.
Free confidential safety planning and referral to emergency shelter, counseling, legal help, and a Coordinated Entry assessment. You do not have to leave an abusive person before calling. Call 911 for immediate danger.
Illinois Domestic Violence Hotline

entries.title: Sarah's Circle — women experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Phone: 773-728-1014. Weekday meals, showers, laundry, hygiene, clothing, mail, computers, and case management for women age 18+, including trans women.
For emergency shelter, call 311; daytime services do not guarantee placement in Sarah's Circle interim housing.
Sarah's Circle
entries.address: Daytime center: 4838 North Sheridan Road, Chicago, IL 60640

entries.title: Covenant House Illinois — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 312-759-7878.
LGBTQ-affirming youth drop-in and housing linkages with food, showers, laundry, mail, storage, ID help, health, counseling, education, and employment services.
Covenant House — get help
entries.address: Address: 2934 West Lake Street, Chicago, IL 60612

entries.title: Broadway Youth Center — LGBTQ+ and unstably housed ages 12–24
entries.description:
Phone: 773-388-1600. Drop-in hours vary Monday–Friday.
Primary and sexual health care, mental wellness, social services, community, and housing-support connections regardless of ability to pay. Check the current daily schedule.
Broadway Youth Center hours
entries.address: Address: 1023 West Irving Park Road, Chicago, IL 60613

entries.title: Children and teens under 18
entries.description:
CCBYS shelter and crisis connection: 877-870-2663, 24 hours. National Runaway Safeline: 800-786-2929.
Emergency shelter, counseling, outreach, family support, and referrals for children and teens. If a child is in immediate danger, call 911.
Youth emergency guidance

entries.title: Immigrants, migrants, and refugees
entries.description:
Chicago states that city shelter, food, and medical-care referrals are available regardless of immigration status. Call 311 for shelter and 211 for services and language support.
For immigration legal and social-service providers, use the city resource guide. Do not pay a “notario” or unlicensed person for immigration legal advice.
Chicago Welcoming City resources

entries.title: Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights
entries.description:
Family Support Network referrals for immigration legal services and community support. Use the Coalition's current outreach page for the hotline and information about enforcement concerns.
If detained, do not sign documents you do not understand; ask to speak with a qualified immigration attorney.
Immigrant-rights referrals for unhoused people

entries.title: VA Community Resource and Referral Center
entries.description:
Phone: 312-569-5750. National homeless-veteran hotline: 877-424-3838, 24 hours.
One-stop housing, health and mental-health care, benefits, and employment connections for veterans who are homeless or at risk.
VA Chicago homeless-veteran care
entries.address: Address: 1141 South California Avenue, Chicago, IL

entries.title: PAWS Chicago Crisis Foster Care
entries.description:
Temporary foster care for up to 60 days for an eligible dog or cat when the owner faces homelessness, domestic violence, hospitalization, or another crisis. Veterinary care is provided as needed during placement.
Limits include no more than two pets, no puppies or kittens under one year, and restrictions for aggression or unmanageable medical conditions. Apply and wait for confirmation before making plans.
PAWS Crisis Foster Care

entries.title: Friendship Center — pet food
entries.description:
Cook County residents may request dog or cat food while shopping at the food pantry, while supplies last. There are no ZIP-code or income requirements; households may shop twice each month.
Published pantry hours from June 2026 are Monday and Thursday noon–4 p.m., Tuesday 3–7 p.m., and Friday noon–4 p.m. Confirm before traveling because food and supplies depend on donations.
Current pet-food rules and pantry hours
entries.address: Address: 2709 West Lawrence Avenue, Chicago, IL 60625

entries.title: Pets and shelter placement
entries.description:
Tell 311 or SPARC the species, size, temperament, vaccination status, carrier or leash, and medical needs before accepting placement. Franciscan Outreach publishes a personal-pet room at one specialized shelter, but availability and referral rules change.
Ask about a pet-compatible placement or temporary foster care. Do not abandon an animal to enter shelter.
Franciscan Outreach pet accommodation

entries.title: Verification and corrections
entries.description: This page was verified on November 11, 2026 using City of Chicago, Cook County, Illinois state and federal sources, Chicago Coalition to End Homelessness, and direct provider pages. Capacity and intake rules change. If a service has closed or a detail is wrong, see how to submit a correction. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
